title: Multi-groupBy integration test + parity fixture
description: End-to-end proof that a 3-layer nested aggregation (country ExactValue × freight FixedWidth(100) × orderDate Duration(P3M)) runs through the PG-backed OMS → pkg/index.BuildMapping → pkg/oss/aggregation.Engine pipeline and produces leaf rows whose count / sum / avg metrics match a hand-computed expected map. This fixture documents the exact wire-level response shape Foundry SDK consumers rely on for multi-layer groupBy queries and pins the deterministic seed used by test/integration/aggregation_multigroupby_test.go.

seed.pattern: 5 countries × 3 quarters × 7 prices = 105 orders. Every (country, quarter) combo carries the same 7-row price grid so the inner fixedWidth bucket boundaries are independent of the outer country scope.

groupKeyInvariants.freight: string of the form '[lo,hi)' produced by fmt.Sprintf("[%.0f,%.0f)", lo, lo+width)
groupKeyInvariants.orderDate: RFC3339 bucket start computed as floor(epoch/(90*86400))*(90*86400) in UTC

responseShape.excludedItems: int — count of caller-supplied excludedItems PKs that intersected the post-scope query (US-382)
responseShape.accuracy: "ACCURATE" | "APPROXIMATE" — ACCURATE when no numeric scan exceeded engine.MaxDocScanSize
responseShape.computeUsage: { scannedRows: int64, durationMs: int64, accuracy: string } — per-aggregation cost-and-quality envelope (US-382 superseded the float64 form)

notes: Run the integration test with `go test -tags integration ./test/integration/... -run MultiGroupBy`. It requires Docker for testcontainers.

The duration bucket math floors from the Unix epoch, not calendar quarters. Three 2024 anchor dates — 2024-01-15, 2024-04-15, 2024-07-15 — are chosen because floor(epoch/(90*86400)) maps each to a DISTINCT multiple of 7 776 000 s. Calendar-quarter boundaries would NOT be sufficient by themselves; collisions must be asserted against the flooring contract.

fixedWidth bucket name formatting comes from fmt.Sprintf("[%.0f,%.0f)", lo, lo+width) in getFixedWidthEntries. Any future switch to scientific or locale-sensitive formatting would silently break this fixture — treat the name as a contract, not an implementation detail.

shipCountry uses analyzer.not_analyzed so the facet keys are case-preserved. Switching the analyzer to standard would fold `"UK"` → `"uk"` at index time and `outerCountryOrder` would collapse — the assertion lives in the test to catch that regression.

The seed is deliberately dense (every (country, quarter) emits the same 7-price grid) so that every leaf count / sum / avg is closed-form. A sparser real-world Northwind cut would still work but would require materialising the expected map from the source CSV, not from the test.
